title: GM pushrod V6/V8: misfire or tick from worn cam lobe/lifter roller or collapsed AFM lifter
summary: GM diagnostic tip 19-NA-219 for P0300-P0308 misfires and tick/chirp noises on 2002-2023 GM pushrod V6/V8 engines, including Active Fuel Management lifters.

specs.name: Possible causes listed
specs.value: Worn cam lobe and/or lifter roller, sticking valve, valve leakage, broken valve spring, collapsed AFM lifter

steps.text: Start with the GM service information diagnosis. If that does not isolate the cause, work through the checks below, easiest first.

Find a noisy rocker: during the noise, press with a wooden hammer handle on the valve side, pushrod side and side of each rocker. A change when pressing the valve side points to that cylinder's lifter or cam lobe.

Disconnect the coils and injectors on one bank, run the engine with that valve cover off, back off one rocker a couple of turns and listen. If the noise stops and spring, pushrod and rocker are fine, suspect a worn lifter roller or cam lobe.
Measure lift at the pushrod side of each rocker and compare with others on the same bank. Low or no lift on an AFM cylinder (V8: 1, 4, 6, 7; V6: 3, 6) can also mean a collapsed AFM lifter.
On AFM engines (not 2017-2018 models), command AFM on with the scan tool to unlatch those lifters. If the noise stops, it is in the valvetrain of the AFM cylinders.
Inspect lifter rollers and cam lobes through the lifter bores (a bore scope helps) for flat spots, pits, grooves, scoring, gouging, flaking or rust. A good roller does not prove a good lobe.
An AFM lifter that unlocks at start-up gives P0300 and misfires on the AFM cylinders, usually with no noise. One that is mechanically collapsed or stuck adds a steady valvetrain tick.

If a lobe or roller is worn: replace the camshaft and all lifters per service information, plus the plastic lifter guide for the damaged lifter (2010 model year: all guides). On AFM engines also replace the VLOM filter screen under the oil pressure sensor.
L83, L86, LT1 and LT4 engines with an AFM lifter concern follow GM bulletin 15-06-01-002 instead.

body: Oil consumption on GM engines is covered by GM's general oil consumption bulletin series 01-06-01-011, which gives the measurement procedure. The earlier draft of this entry also blamed AFM for oil consumption; that claim was removed because the cited bulletins do not state it.
